subject: people who talk too much
tagline: Neuralink for people who talk too much
one_liner: A cortical implant that ends your sentences before you have finished having them.
brand_voice_notes: Regulated-medical-device register throughout. Every claim is phrased as a clinical outcome, never as a feeling. Talkativeness is treated as a condition with a dosage, not as a personality. No exclamation marks, no reassurance, no second-person encouragement. Numbers are given to one decimal place even when the decimal is meaningless. The leaflet never acknowledges that anything about this is unusual.

hero.sub: Taciten is a cortical throttle indicated for adults whose stories have no observable endpoint. One outpatient procedure, one indefinite subscription, and a measured reduction in the number of times per day you say “anyway, so.”

features.title: Sentence ceiling
features.blurb: Set a hard word limit per utterance. On contact with the ceiling, Taciten closes the sentence for you using the nearest available grammatical exit. In trials, 71.4% of closures landed on “so yeah.”

features.title: Anecdote deduplication
features.blurb: The implant indexes every story you tell and tags it against the listener who heard it. The second time you begin the one about the airport, your jaw is not consulted.

features.title: Floor yield
features.blurb: Taciten monitors the room for a person who has been waiting to speak for more than 4.0 seconds and administers a brief, non-negotiable pause. The pause is not adjustable. The pause is the product.

demo_screen_concept: The clinician-facing Floor Control console, open on a live session: a dinner party, 4 participants, 82 minutes elapsed. Left rail is the wearer's live word-budget meter draining against a 60-word sentence ceiling with a ceiling slider the clinician can drag. Center is the participant roster with horizontal airtime bars (the wearer at 61.2%, everyone else compressed underneath) and a live suppression toggle per participant. Right is the Held Utterances queue: things the implant intercepted before they reached the jaw, each with a reason code (CEILING, REPEAT-ANECDOTE, INTERRUPT, FLOOR-YIELD), a timestamp, and a transcript fragment that can be expanded, released back to the wearer, or discarded permanently. Bottom strip is the dosing schedule for the next 6 hours.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the design direction is a pharmaceutical leaflet: panel 1 is typographic and diagrammatic, and a photograph would break the print conceit. Demo subject assets skipped because demo_screen_concept is a clinician console (meters, roster bars, a held-utterance queue), which is not photo-shaped. Full budget went to the three testimonial headshots, shot as leaflet patient photography: flat medical-office lighting on a cold bleached grey-green backdrop matching the page stock. 3 of a possible 4 images generated, all accepted on the first attempt.

items.prompt: Editorial clinical portrait photograph in the style of a pharmaceutical patient information leaflet. One middle-aged adult, broad slightly over-friendly face relaxed into deliberate neutrality, short sandy hair, plain charcoal quarter-zip pullover, shoulders square to camera, seated upright. Flat even medical-office lighting from the front, no drama, no rim light. Plain seamless backdrop in cold bleached grey-green #EAEEEC. A faint deep regulatory green #00594F in the shadows of the clothing. Restrained, documentary, slightly airless corporate-healthcare mood. Sharp focus on the eyes, shallow depth of field. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no signage, no name badges, no rendered UI screens.
items.judge: Pass. Subject and wardrobe correct, backdrop sits on the page stock, expression is deadpan rather than smiling, no text artifacts, skin and fabric read photographic rather than rendered.

design_direction.style: Pharmaceutical patient-information leaflet, cold-bleached paper daylight mode. The page is staged as the regulatory insert folded out of a medicine carton for an implant that the manufacturer would prefer you think of as a drug. One bleached stock (#EAEEEC, a cold paper with a faint green cast, never warm, never cream) runs the whole page in a single light mode, with no dark variant, no glass, no backdrop blur, no clay volume, no bento lattice, no newsprint, no moulded plastic, no plaster, no banknote plate, no enamel, no sprocket rail, no leaded came and no stained glass. Nothing on the page casts a shadow, because print does not cast shadows. There are exactly two spot inks, deep regulatory green (#00594F) and contraindication vermilion (#D93B1E), and every coloured element on the page is one of those two at full strength or the same ink at 8 to 14 percent as a tint block; no third hue is ever introduced and no ink is ever gradated except a 4 percent grey along a fold crease. The organising move is the fold: the page is divided into leaflet panels separated by full-bleed crease lines, each a 1px muted rule flanked by a 12px vertical gradient at 4 percent black on one side only, so sections arrive as panels of folded paper rather than as cards in a grid. The core motif is the blister well: a stadium-shaped cavity, border-radius 999px on a 2px inset green hairline with a 6 percent green tint fill, used for feature numbers, pricing tier marks, perk bullets and the demo's status pills, so every discrete item reads as one dose punched into foil. The second motif is the black-box warning: a 2px vermilion frame with a solid vermilion caps header bar, reserved for exactly one block per page and never decorative. The third motif is the metadata strip: a tabular row of caps micro-labels at 10px with 0.14em tracking (LOT, REV, ROUTE, SCHEDULE) separated by hairline verticals, run under every major heading. Border radius is 0 everywhere except blister wells. Rules are 1px and only ever muted, green or vermilion. All section headers are Barlow Condensed uppercase preceded by a solid green square carrying a white section numeral. Pictograms are inline SVG at a single 1.5px stroke, never filled, never emoji.
design_direction.archetype: landing page for a regulated medical device, composed as a product information insert
design_direction.motion_vocab: Print has almost no motion, so the page moves like paper and nothing else. Panels resolve on scroll with a 180ms opacity and 2px upward translate, staggered 40ms per child. Blister wells depress 1px on press and return. The black-box warning's top rule draws in left to right over 240ms once, on first view. Nothing scales, nothing floats, nothing parallaxes, no duration exceeds 240ms, and every transition is skipped wholesale under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Panel 1 is full-bleed leaflet front. Product name set in Barlow Condensed uppercase at clamp(3.5rem, 13vw, 8.5rem) with tight 0.88 leading, sitting on a 2px green rule. Directly under the rule, a strength line in mono-tabular caps reading the route and dose the way a carton would. Body copy sits in a two-column measure at 900px and above, collapsing to one column below, with a right-hand metadata rail carrying lot number, revision code and an instruction to read the leaflet before speaking. The primary CTA is a solid green block with square corners and caps tracking, sized like a pharmacy label rather than a web button. Hero carries no photograph; the panel is typographic and diagrammatic by design.
design_direction.anti_sameness_check: Checked against the previous 7 entries (stained glass, risograph, microfilm carrel, injection-moulded console, gallery wall label, intaglio banknote, vitreous enamel signage). No collision on style archetype, palette or font pairing.
